title: Topical Intranasal Anesthetic Block for Reducing the Pain of Botulinum Toxin Injections for Chronic Migraine
official: Topical Intranasal Anesthetic Block for Reducing the Pain of Botulinum Toxin Injections for Chronic Migraine: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Crossover Pilot Study
summary: People find the injections used in onabotulinumtoxinA (Botox®) uncomfortable. This study will test whether putting a small piece of cotton soaked with 4% lidocaine (a numbing medicine) inside the front of each nostril for 5 minutes before the injections reduces injection pain compared with cotton soaked in saline (salt water).
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Aged ≥18 years
* Any gender
* Able to provide informed consent
* Meets clinical criteria for onabotulinumtoxinA for chronic migraine (minimum of 2 days of disability per month due to facial or headache pain, or 8 headache days per month, or more than 15 headaches per month)
* Scheduled for modified PREEMPT injections at the clinical site

Exclusion Criteria:

* Aged \< 18 years
* Trigeminal neuralgia, cluster headache, or other primary headache disorders as dominant diagnosis
* Not able to provide informed consent
* Known allergy/hypersensitivity to lidocaine or amide anesthetics
* Pregnancy/lactation
* Inability to tolerate intranasal nasal cotton pledgets
* Significant nasal pathology at placement site
